key_insight: First-principles calculations predict ferroelectric ground states in 11 of 15 [111]-oriented perovskite-oxide superlattices, with octahedral rotations significantly altering ferroelectric properties in some cases.
engineering_relevance: The findings inform orientation and composition choices for ferroelectric oxide heterostructures, but do not establish solar-cell performance or involve AI.
method: Calculate ground-state structures of 15 free-standing oxide superlattices from first principles.
Analyze zone-center phonons, ferroelectric distortions, octahedral rotations, and force constants.
Compare thermodynamic stability for [111] and [100] growth orientations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ferroelectric ground states in 11 of 15 calculated superlattices and identifies both polar and octahedral-rotation distortions with Γ-point phonons.
watch_item: Predictions for free-standing structures require validation under realistic substrate constraints; no photovoltaic evaluation is reported.
paper_title: Properties of [111]-oriented ferroelectric superlattices based on oxides with a perovskite structure
